articles.title: ‘Check the weight of balls too’: Deepak Chahar tells authorities
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Soon after he picked up a haul of three for 13 in four overs to help Rajasthan beat Bengal by six wickets in a must-win game at the Wankhede
articles.body: MUMBAI: Soon after he picked up a haul of three for 13 in four overs to help Rajasthan beat Bengal by six wickets in a must-win game at the Wankhede Stadium and qualify for the Super League stage of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, veteran pacer Deepak Chahar, who completed 200 wickets in T20 cricket on Thursday, made a plea to the game's authorities on the behalf of swing bowlers like him: 'Check the weight of the Kookaburra ball.'According to the 34-year-old quick, in recent years, white-ball games, especially in the IPL, are perhaps being played with heavier Kookaburra balls that don't swing that much, which reduces the effectiveness of a swing bowler like him."Overall, the ball is swinging a little less these days, whether in the IPL, domestic cricket or any other game. I suddenly found out that the ball has a lot of weight. About a month back, one day I just happened to check the weight of 15 new (Kookaburra) balls. I felt that the weight of the balls was a little extra. So, I got 15 balls checked (for weight). None of them weighed 153 grams (the permitted weight). 153 grams. I asked an umpire and a match referee. They said that the balls should weigh between 153 and 161 grams. However, all the balls were between 164-171 grams," Chahar told reporters at the Wankhede Stadium."They (the umpires) are not checking (the weight of the ball). The frame or shape of the ball is checked. The size of the ball is checked, but not the weight. I have asked for it to be checked. I think it should be checked. If the bat is being checked, the frame is being checked, the ball is being checked in the frame. All the 12 balls that we get to select for the match should be within the norms in terms of weight. If it is heavier (then the allowed weight), then it is wrong,” he reiterated.The Rajasthan skipper, who has taken 47 wickets for India in 38 white-ball internationals, raised this issue in the captains' meeting with the BCCI match referee and umpires before this edition of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. The feedback that he got was good."I raised the issue of the weight of the balls during the captains meeting before SMAT. They (the other captains, match referee and umpires) said that they raised a good point because the weight of the ball is not checked. When the umpires check the size of the ball before the match, they check whether it is of the right size or not. But the weight of the ball is not checked. So, they said that if someone has raised a point for the first time, we will forward it," Chahar told reporters here.The seamer, who has taken 31 wickets in 25 T20Is, and 16 wickets in 13 ODIs, pointed out that for swing bowlers like him, there was more help in SMAT, where matches start at 9am, rather than in the IPL, where wickets are "very flat." "You get a bit of swing in the Mushtaq Ali, but not much in the IPL. The wickets are very flat in IPL, where only one pitch is used for one match. In SMAT, in the first two matches of the day, there is a little moisture in the pitch. In the first match, there is a little movement available too.Chahar hasn't spoken to the other bowlers, who he says are unaware about the weight of the cricket balls being heavier, about the issue. "No, I don't think anyone checks the size of the ball. I have seen that if I get 12 balls in the match, only five-six balls will have the right weight, if they are checked. Otherwise, most of the balls are a little heavy," Chahar said.Has he raised this issue before the IPL? "Before the IPL, I will raise the point that we should get 12 balls of the same weight in the match," Chahar asserted.Chahar revealed that a couple of years back, he had asked to increase the number of balls provided for each team to 12 from six during the IPL, an appeal that was 'accepted' by the BCCI pretty quickly once cricket great and former India captain MS Dhoni intervened at Chahar's request to his former Chennai Super Kings skipper."I had also raised this point in 2024. Earlier, we used to get (only) six balls( to select from). Out of that, four-five balls used to be (too) heavy. (Only) One and a half ball would be good. If it is heavy, then the swing is less. I had told Mahibhai (Dhoni) about this. Mahibhai went and mentioned this in a conference. So next month, we started getting 12 balls. This must have happened in the IPL. It changed immediately," Chahar recalled.Chahar claimed that lighter cricket balls swing much more. "You have to give a ball of 148 to 150 grams in the IPL. In the Gulf, they use a ball which weighs 148 grams. You see how much swing they get there. A difference of five-grams six makes a massive difference in swinging the ball. If a ball is 10 grams too heavy, it will go slow and the swing will be less. I am not saying anything wrong. You should get a ball of the same weight as the norms. But in Mushtaq Ali, things have been better," the speedster said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Baz pulled me aside': Tom Banton recalls emotional moment he was named England captain
articles.summary: Tom Banton is set to achieve a major milestone in his international career after being named England captain for the fifth and final T20I against
articles.body: Tom Banton is set to achieve a major milestone in his international career after being named England captain for the fifth and final T20I against Australia. The 27-year-old described the moment as emotional, admitting that he initially struggled to react when head coach Brendon McCullum informed him about the decision. Banton will lead England in the series finale in Canberra on December 2'I was pretty emotional'Speaking about the moment, Banton revealed that McCullum, popularly known as 'Baz', pulled him aside at the airport and shared the news."I was pretty emotional, a little bit, when I got told. It's a great honour and a great privilege, and something I'm really looking forward to," Banton said.He further explained how McCullum personally informed him about the responsibility."Baz did it actually in the airport. He just pulled me aside and told me. I didn't really know how to react, to be honest. But yeah, to be told you'll be captaining your country in any format is a real privilege," he added.Why will Tom Banton captain England against Australia?England's captaincy change comes after two major developments during their ongoing Australia tour. Regular skipper Harry Brook is set to leave Australia after the fourth T20I to prepare for England's upcoming Test commitments against South Africa. Will Jacks was expected to take over the captaincy for the final match but suffered a broken hand during the opening T20I against Australia, ruling him out of the remainder of the white-ball tour.With both players unavailable, Banton has been handed the responsibility of leading England in the series finale.Tom Banton's journey to England captaincyBanton made his international debut for England in 2019 and has since featured across formats. The Somerset batter has experienced ups and downs in his international career but has continued to work his way back into the national setup.The captaincy opportunity marks a significant moment for the 27-year-old, who will now get the chance to lead his country on the international stage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Mohammed Azharuddeen achieved a remarkable century during the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy match against Himachal Pradesh. He scored 101 runs off just 57 balls, h...
articles.body:
NEW DELHI: Kerala batter Mohammed Azharuddeen came up with a special gesture for captain Sanju Samson after scoring a century in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy match against Himachal Pradesh on Thursday. After reaching his hundred, Azharuddeen turned his bat towards the camera, showing the name 'Samson' written on it. The camera then moved towards Samson, who was sitting in the dressing room, and captured his reaction to the gesture. Azharuddeen reached his century in just 56 balls, hitting a six off Arpit Guleria to bring up the milestone. His innings included eight fours and six sixes.

Kerala won the toss and elected to bat at the PCA International Cricket Stadium, Ground A. Azharuddeen led the charge with a brilliant 101 off 57 balls as Kerala posted a massive 268/4 in 20 overs. The wicketkeeper-batter struck at 177.19 and shared a solid 82-run opening partnership with Rohan Kunnummal, who scored 35 off 16 balls.

Samson also made a quick contribution, scoring 44 off 21 balls with five fours and two sixes. Vishnu Vinod added 22 off 11 balls. Salman Nizar remained unbeaten on 26 off 15 balls, while Abdul Basith provided a late boost with an unbeaten 24 off just five deliveries. Basith smashed three sixes and a four at a strike rate of 480. Kerala finished with 268/4 at a run rate of 13.40. For Himachal Pradesh, Mridul Surroch picked up two wickets, while Aryaman Singh Dhaliwal and Arpit Guleria took one wicket each.

articles.title: 'I have no regrets': Mohammed Shami opens up on Test retirement, says he's happy with what he received
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Mohammed Shami didn't have a particularly fruitful outing in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy, finishing with four wickets in seven matches@43.00,
articles.body: MUMBAI: Mohammed Shami didn't have a particularly fruitful outing in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy, finishing with four wickets in seven matches@43.00, at an economy rate of 8.60. On Thursday, he conceded 0-19 in three overs, as Bengal lost their must-win final league match to Rajasthan by six wickets to crash out of the tournament.However, the veteran pacer, who announced his Test retirement about a month back, has moved beyond purely worrying about his own performances. Shami was pleased to see the emergence of some young talent in the BCCI’s domestic tournament."Overall, it was a good outing, because I got to see a lot of things, a few youngsters in our team. I got to see some new talent as well. And I hope that from this tournament, we will get to see new faces in the auctions. I am getting to see good talent and skill. Hopefully, some new guys emerge from this season," Shami told reporters at the Wankhede Stadium on Thursday.The 36-year-old fast bowler may have hung his boots in Test cricket, but he has no plans of slowing down. The veteran India fast bowler is keen to continue playing white-ball cricket, and in the Ranji Trophy for Bengal.For Shami, the motivation to keep playing still remains the same as before. “I have said this before: I will continue playing white-ball cricket, and if required, I will play red-ball cricket as well for (maintaining my) fitness. I’ve been doing this for the last 15-20 years. It’s the same old routine. Nothing new,” he said.Despite getting a raw deal from the national selectors for the past couple of years, Shami has no regrets about how his Test journey ended, after he enjoyed considerable success in the format, taking 229 wickets in 64 Tests@27.71, with six fivers, between 2012-2023.It was only last season when Shami showcased what magic he can conjure up with the red ball, taking eight for 90 against Jammu & Kashmir in the Ranji Trophy semifinal. However, nine months later, the ace pacer announced his Test retirement. Rated as one of India’s best fast bowlers ever, Shami has now learnt to brush off any disappointment or regret and has made peace with what life has given him.“I have no regrets. Whatever I got was what was destined for me. You get only what the Almighty has written in your destiny. I am happy with whatever I have received. Now, I will play as much as I am destined to and enjoy it,” he said.The fast bowler is also keen to keep playing for Bengal in domestic cricket, where he believes his experience can be valuable to younger players. Shami sees this as an opportunity to give something back. “There’s no question of losing motivation. As long as you love cricket and enjoy playing the game, you should continue. I have said this before as well. As long as you are enjoying it, you should keep playing. That is my motivation. Also, if we can help a few youngsters in some way, that would be even better. Especially when you play for your state, experience matters a lot,” he said.Will he play in the Vijay Hazare Trophy too? “Sure,” pat came the reply, before Shami outlined that he now had the option to “pick and choose” his matches. “I have the option of picking and choosing. I can decide which matches I want to play and which ones I don’t. There is no pressure. Hopefully, I’m fit for the season ahead and things keep going well,” he said.While a return to international white-ball cricket remains a possibility, Shami is not spending his time thinking about the next World Cup cycle. The 2027 ODI World Cup and the 2028 T20 World Cup may be on the horizon, but Shami would rather concentrate on what is immediately in front of him. “I have stopped thinking about all these things. Right now, my focus is on my game. Whatever decision they (the national selectors) take will be better. I just want to focus on staying fit, keep playing for my state (Bengal) and enjoy the sport,” Shami asserted.‘Avoid early starts in SMAT’Shami concurred with former India players Irfan Pathan and Wasim Jaffer that 9am, or 8am starts in case of Kolkata, where Mumbai are playing their league matches, are too early for SMAT games."I have also said this before, that the T20 format (games) should start at around 12-1pm. If you are playing two matches everyday, then those games should be held in the afternoon and evening. Because in the morning, there is a lot of dew and moisture in the wicket this season. So, I think the toss becomes a (big) factor somewhere," Shami felt.Backs call for using saliva on the ballDuring the 2025 Champions Trophy in Dubai, Shami had appealed to the cricket authorities to revoke the ban on saliva in order to allow pace bowlers to rediscover swing and reverse swing. It wasn't surprising, therefore, that Shami backed India captain Shubman Gill’s suggestion after India's drawn test against New Zealand at Wellington that bowlers should be allowed to apply saliva on the ball since covid was long gone.“I back Shubman’s statement on allowing bowlers to apply saliva on the ball. Kuchh toh maza aye red ball mein... (Red-ball cricket should have some added fun!),” Shami said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: KOLKATA: For the second consecutive season Bengal failed to make the knockout stage of the Syed Mushtaq Ali (T20) tournament after going down to Rajasthan
articles.body: KOLKATA: For the second consecutive season Bengal failed to make the knockout stage of the Syed Mushtaq Ali (T20) tournament after going down to Rajasthan by six wickets in their last Elite Group ‘A’ match at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on Thursday.Although Baroda lost their last group stage match to Karnataka, they qualified as the group topper with 20 points. As Bengal and Rajasthan shared the same number of points (16) before Thursday’s clash, the winner of the tie stood to progress as the second-best side from the group. But Bengal failed to make it count when it mattered. Another batting failure saw them score below par 157/9 in their 20 overs after electing to bat first on winning the toss.Opener Abhishek Tomar’s well-crafted half-century helped Rajasthan romp home in just 16.2 overs scoring 162/4 and progress to the next stage.It was a bit surprising to see skipper Abhimanyu Easwaran opting to bat first on a lively pitch and Bengal were quickly reduced to 32/4 inside the first five overs losing Abishek Porel (0), Aditya Purohit (1), Easwaran (26) and Shashank Singh (2). Shakib Gandhi and Karan Lal did try to arrest the slide being involved in a 48-ball 73-ball fifth-wicket stand, but once Lal was run out for 28, Gandhi got little support from the lower order as he was the last man to depart for a 43-ball 69. Rajasthan pacers Deepak Chahar and Arafat Khan picked up three wickets each.Bengal began well, reducing Rajasthan to 37/3 by the sixth over, but some poor fielding saw them lose the initiative. Mahipal Lomror and Tomar took control of the chase with a 119-run fourth-wicket stand. When Lomror departed for a 35-ball 74-run innings, Rajasthan were already within touching distance of victory and they achieved it without further hiccups.Brief scores: Bengal 157/9 in 20 ovs (Shakir Gandhi 69; Deepak Chahar 3/13, Arafat Khan 3/36). articles.body: NEW DELHI: India will look to bounce back and keep their World Test Championship (WTC) final hopes alive when they take on New Zealand in the second and final Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch from November 27. After dominating large parts of the series opener in Wellington but failing to force a result, Shubman Gill's side will be eager to turn their performance into a victory and avoid another setback in their campaign.India's hopes of securing a top-two finish in the WTC standings suffered a blow after the drawn first Test left them fourth. Even that, however, may not be enough, with India also dependent on other results.Bowling coach Morne Morkel has urged the players not to get overwhelmed by the pressure of reaching the WTC final and instead focus on delivering their best cricket in Christchurch. India's batting impressed in Wellington, with six of their top seven registering half-centuries, but the bowling attack fell five wickets short of securing victory.New Zealand, meanwhile, will look to build on their resilient performance in the series opener. articles.summary: India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant unexpectedly joins a club game in Christchurch before the second Test against New Zealand and scores 54 off 21 balls.
articles.body:
India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant made a surprise appearance for a club team in Christchurch under the false name 'Stan Stan'.

Pant, 29, played for the Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones and smashed 54 from 21 balls in a 16-run win.

His appearance came a day before India's second Test against New Zealand, which begins at the Hagley Oval at 22:00 GMT on Thursday.

Open House player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald that he had seen Pant on an electric bike in the city and approached him, saying that his team were a player short.

Safi also said that Pant was not immediately recognised by many on either side, and he turned up in a purple tracksuit and had to borrow kit.

New Zealand captain Tom Latham said Pant's appearance was "brilliant" and showed his "real character", while India bowling coach and former South Africa quick Morne Morkel said he "nearly fell off my chair" when he saw the footage that circulated on social media.

The first Test in Wellington ended in a high-scoring draw, where Pant scored 128 in India's only innings of 720-9.

Pant is regarded as one of the world's most entertaining cricketers, and has scored 3,853 runs in his 53 Tests at an average just shy of 45.

Of those to have scored more than 2,000 Test runs for India, only Virender Sehwag and Kapil Dev have a better strike-rate than Pant's 74.43.

articles.title: Jaydev Unadkat scripts history with stunning No. 11 knock, smashes T20 world record in SMAT
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Jaydev Unadkat produced a remarkable batting effort from an unlikely position, becoming the highest-scoring No.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jaydev Unadkat produced a remarkable batting effort from an unlikely position, becoming the highest-scoring No. 11 batter in men's T20 cricket history during Saurashtra's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) clash against Tamil Nadu at the Holkar Stadium in Indore on Thursday. The Saurashtra captain smashed 40 off just 26 balls, surpassing the previous record of 35 not out held by England's Danny Briggs.Unadkat struck three fours and two sixes and shared a sensational 62-run partnership for the 10th wicket with Chetan Sakariya. The pair revived Saurashtra's chase after they had slumped to 92/9 while pursuing a target of 193. However, their late resistance could not prevent a 38-run defeat, with Saurashtra bowled out for 154 in 16.4 overs.Unadkat tops all-time No. 11 batting chartsUnadkat's 40 is now the highest individual score by a No. 11 batter in men's T20 cricket. Briggs had held the record with an unbeaten 35 for Adelaide Strikers against Hobart Hurricanes in 2020. Dominic Drakes is third on the list with an unbeaten 34 for St Kitts and Nevis Patriots against Barbados Tridents in 2019.Belgium's Khalid Ahmadi (31 not out against Malta in 2021) and Afghanistan's Mujeeb Ur Rahman (27 for Brisbane Heat against Adelaide Strikers in 2018) complete the top five.The 62-run stand between Unadkat and Sakariya is also the joint second-highest partnership for the 10th wicket in T20 cricket. They matched the effort of Khengar Ahir and Nikunj Ahir, who added 62 for Panama against Argentina in 2021. The record remains a 63-run stand between Grant Elliott and Zulfiqar Babar for Quetta Gladiators in the 2016 Pakistan Super League.Punjab qualify as Saurashtra crash outEarlier, Tamil Nadu posted 192/8 after being put into bat, with Sunny Sandhu leading the late charge. He smashed six sixes in a 17-ball 44, while Andre Siddarth (38), Balasubramaniam Sachin (37) and R Rajkumar (36) made useful contributions. Sakariya claimed 3/37 for Saurashtra.Sandhu then struck twice in the opening over of the chase, removing Vishvaraj Jadeja and Harvansh Singh. He finished with 4/43, while R Sai Kishore took 3/19 to bowl Saurashtra out.The defeat ended Saurashtra's hopes of reaching the Super League stage after they had won their first four matches before suffering three consecutive defeats. Punjab, meanwhile, had done their part earlier in the day by chasing down a target of 152 in just 13.1 overs. They moved past Saurashtra on points and net run rate to secure qualification from Elite Group B, while Tamil Nadu signed off their campaign with a win.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: It's all over! Sri Lanka A crush India A's Asia Cup Rising Stars dream with stunning chase
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India A's Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign came to a crushing end on Thursday as Sri Lanka A produced a breathtaking batting display to storm
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A's Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign came to a crushing end on Thursday as Sri Lanka A produced a breathtaking batting display to storm into the final with an emphatic eight-wicket victory in the semifinal. Chasing a challenging target of 318, the Islanders romped home with eight wickets and 9.3 overs to spare, exposing India's bowling weaknesses and underlining their batting firepower.The foundation of the remarkable chase was laid by openers Sineth Jayawardena (105 off 70 balls) and Lasith Croospulle (116 off 107), who launched a relentless assault on the Indian attack. Both batters brought up centuries as Sri Lanka seized control of the contest, making light work of a target that had appeared imposing when India finished their innings at 317/8.India had an early opportunity to break the opening stand, but Tanush Kotian dropped Sineth at backward point off his very first delivery. The reprieve proved extremely costly as the Sri Lankan opener made India pay with a match-defining innings. Harshit Rana and Arshad Khan struggled to contain the onslaught, with the pace attack unable to create sustained pressure.Sri Lankan openers dismantle India's bowling attackSineth took the aggressive route, particularly against Arshad, while Croospulle initially played the supporting role. Once the openers settled in, the runs flowed freely and India's bowlers struggled to find answers. The pair's centuries effectively took the game away from India A, who had little control over the proceedings for much of the chase.There was a brief phase when India's spinners managed to slow the scoring and create some uncertainty. However, Croospulle and Nishan Madushka (58 not out off 56 balls) steadied the innings with a crucial partnership, ensuring there was no late twist. Sri Lanka continued to bat with confidence and completed the chase in commanding fashion.The scale of the victory reflected the gulf between the two sides on the day. Sri Lanka's batters attacked without hesitation, while India's bowling unit lacked the penetration and discipline required to defend a total of 317.Nadeem's late flourish lifts India to 317Earlier, Shahbaz Nadeem's unbeaten 54 helped India A recover from a middle-order wobble and post 317/8. The left-hander struck four sixes in a 48-ball knock and shared a valuable 73-run seventh-wicket partnership with Tanush Kotian, who contributed 28.India had made a flying start through Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma, who added 80 for the opening wicket. Sooryavanshi, fresh from his record-breaking 204 in the previous match, scored 40 off 26 balls, hitting four fours and three sixes before mistiming a pull off Janith Liyanage.Abhishek carried the momentum with 78 off 63 balls, including 11 fours and a six, while captain Tilak Varma made 53 off 66 deliveries. Their 79-run second-wicket stand kept India on course for a substantial total, but the middle order could not build on their contributions.Lahiru Samarakoon dismissed Abhishek with a slower delivery, while Ravindu Fernando accounted for Tilak. With wickets falling at regular intervals, India needed Nadeem's late assault to cross the 300-run mark.However, Sri Lanka's extraordinary chase ensured that India's fighting total was nowhere near enough. The Islanders will now head into Sunday's final brimming with confidence as they await their opponents, who will emerge from the other semifinal between Pakistan A and Bangladesh A.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: If Mohammed Siraj is world-class, why is he out?
articles.summary: Mohammed Siraj is going through a difficult phase and finds himself out of India’s playing XI even in conditions that suit his bowling style, but bowling
articles.body: Mohammed Siraj is going through a difficult phase and finds himself out of India’s playing XI even in conditions that suit his bowling style, but bowling coach Morne Morkel has no doubts about the pacer’s quality.Ahead of the second Test against New Zealand, Morkel threw his weight behind Siraj, stressing that selection was beyond the bowler’s control and that the immediate priority was to take stock of his game and find a way back.“For me, he is bowling well. He is a world-class bowler. Sometimes selection decisions are tough to take,” Morkel said.The former South Africa pacer revealed that his message to Siraj has been to simplify things rather than obsess over selection.“The conversation I had with him was: ‘Listen, let’s strip it back a little bit. Where are we at the moment? What do we need to improve and where can we get better?’”Morkel added that Siraj, as a senior member, also had a role to play even when not in the XI.“Selection is something we can’t really control. All we can control is putting our energy into the guys who are playing,” he said. “At the same time, he can take stock of his own game, where he is at and what is going to be his best path back into the team. That comes down to grit and taking responsibility.”But the bigger question is: should Siraj’s performances in Asian conditions be the yardstick for judging his suitability for New Zealand?Would the same principle be applied to a batter? Had Shubman Gill or Yashasvi Jaiswal endured three ducks across two Tests in Sri Lanka, would they have been dropped in New Zealand?The numbers make Siraj’s omission intriguing. Since his heroics in England, he has played seven Tests, all in the subcontinent, taking 21 wickets at 21.28 and a strike rate of 44.2, considerably better than his career strike rate of 51.Then there are the two Tests in Sri Lanka, which appear to have counted heavily against him.At Galle, Siraj returned 1/29 and 1/15 from nine overs in each innings. Fellow seamer Prasidh Krishna took 1/47 and 2/16. At the SSC, Siraj had 1/33 and 1/26, while Prasidh returned 3/52 and 1/57.Here’s the context, though.India enforced the follow-on at SSC after spending 89.4 overs in the field in Sri Lanka’s first innings.One criticism of Siraj in Sri Lanka was the drop in his pace. Didn’t India’s quicks, including the great Jasprit Bumrah, experience something similar on the sluggish Basin Reserve surface in Wellington?Interestingly, Morkel cautioned against viewing speed-gun readings in isolation.“I wouldn’t read too much into the speed gun from the last game because of the nature of the surface,” he said. “The data and the black-and-white facts showed that the wicket lost a lot of pace quite early in the Test.”The SSC surface, too, had lost pace as the Test progressed and was more conducive to spinners, but even they couldn’t succeed.For Morkel, the larger issue is India learning to operate better with the Kookaburra once its initial hardness and movement disappear.“My experience from playing 16 years with a Kookaburra ball is that you need to make that new ball count,” he said. “You need to get the ball in the right areas and sometimes be a bit braver with your lengths and lines, even if that means going for a few runs.”Morkel also defended Anshul Kamboj from criticism after Wellington, arguing that judging a fast bowler on pace and returns without factoring in the surface would be unfair.And therein lies the contradiction surrounding Siraj.If conditions must be factored in while assessing Kamboj at Wellington, doesn’t Siraj deserve similar allowance for his performances on unresponsive surfaces in Sri Lanka?Meanwhile, the tall and quick Gurnoor Brar is pushing for a Test debut, with Morkel admitting his pace and bounce could be well suited to New Zealand conditions.As India grapple with a new bowling combination, a bowler described as world-class is wondering whether he will figure in it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
On Monday, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips held firm for 43 overs to earn the Black Caps a hard-fought draw in Wellington after India posted a record score of 720-9d.

Pant scored 128 in that Test, with the second Test between the sides beginning on Thursday at Hagley Oval.

Yet, footage has since emerged of Pant playing for club side Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones on Wednesday, scoring 54 off 21 balls under the name 'Stan Stan' to seal a 16-run victory.

"Did he play?! How'd he go?" Latham said at his New Zealand press conference. "That's brilliant!

"It's great. He's obviously a real character of the game, is Rishabh.

"It's great for him to be giving his experience back to LMS (Last Man Standing) teams!"

Pant has scored 3,853 runs in his 53 Tests for India, averaging just below of 45.

The 29-year-old also boasts a strike-rate of 74.43, which is bettered only by Virender Sehwag and Kapil Dev among players to have scored more than 2,000 Test runs for India.

articles.title: Sandpapergate: Cricket Australia outlines terms of reference for independent hearing into scandal
articles.summary: Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England.
articles.body:
Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England.

The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4-0.

Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged.

Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them.

All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out.

The scandal was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography. In it, Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about ball-tampering in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town.

The four frontline bowlers in that 2018 team - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and current Test captain Pat Cummins - have always denied knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball.

Cummins has called Khawaja's recollection of events "nonsense".

However, former team-mates David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of three players who were banned for their part in the scandal, alongside Steve Smith - have backed Khawaja's version of events.

"All participants in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa, including players and support staff, will be invited to take part in the Independent Forum, as will CA management and directors at that time," Cricket Australia said.

"While all involved will be encouraged to participate, there will be no compulsion to do so. All materials supplied will be treated as confidential unless otherwise stated by the participant and no sanctions will be retrospectively applied.

"Participants can choose to attend the Independent Forum in person, online and/or provide information via written accounts or through relevant documents and materials."

articles.body: A contentious umpiring decision sparked a heated reaction from India A players during their ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 semi-final against Sri Lanka A in Doha on Thursday.The incident occurred during the 24th over of Sri Lanka A's 318-run chase when Shahbaz Ahmed appealed for an LBW against opener Lasith Croospulle. However, the on-field umpire turned down the appeal, leaving the Indian players visibly frustrated.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was quick to approach the umpire, questioning whether Croospulle had got an inside edge. Captain Tilak Varma also expressed his displeasure before asking the youngster to move away from the official.Shahbaz, meanwhile, appeared stunned by the decision and was seen holding his head in disbelief after the appeal was rejected.What happened during the controversial LBW appeal?Shahbaz delivered a skiddy ball on a good length, which struck Croospulle on the pads as the batter attempted to flick it towards the leg side. The bowler immediately appealed, with Sooryavanshi and Tilak joining in. However, the umpire remained unmoved and reportedly indicated that the delivery was going down the leg side.The front-on replay made it difficult to determine whether Croospulle had managed an inside edge. While the Indian players believed they had a strong case for an LBW, the available footage did not conclusively establish whether the batter had edged the ball. The decision triggered a brief exchange between the Indian players and the umpire.Centuries from Croospulle, Jayawardena power Sri Lanka A into finalSri Lanka A eventually defeated India A by eight wickets to book their place in the final of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026. Chasing 318, Sri Lanka A reached the target in just 41.3 overs, with Lasith Croospulle scoring 116 off 107 deliveries and Sineth Jayawardena smashing 105 off 70 balls.The opening pair stitched together a 174-run partnership to put Sri Lanka A in command. Nishan Madushka then remained unbeaten on 58 to guide his side home. Earlier, India A posted 317/8 in their 50 overs, with Abhishek Sharma (78), Tilak Varma (53) and Shahbaz Ahmed (54 not out) scoring half-centuries. articles.title: 'We are talking about Mohammed Siraj, but what about Ravindra Jadeja?': Sunil Gavaskar questions India's 2nd Test selection
articles.summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has questioned India's decision to leave out Ravindra Jadeja for the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch.
articles.body: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has questioned India's decision to leave out Ravindra Jadeja for the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch. He felt the experienced all-rounder's bowling could have been useful on a pitch that is expected to offer little help to spinners.India's team selection has sparked a debate, with pacer Mohammed Siraj also missing out on the playing XI. However, Gavaskar felt Jadeja's omission deserved equal attention.Speaking on Sony Sports Network after the toss, Gavaskar pointed out that Jadeja has been one of India's most successful bowlers in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle. He also said the left-arm spinner could have made an impact on the fourth and fifth days of the Test."Well, we are only talking about Siraj, but what about Jadeja? He is India's third-highest wicket-taker in this WTC cycle. I do believe his spin would've been pretty useful on the fourth and fifth days. He is someone who is known to grip and turn the ball on placid pitches. So, tough luck for him as well as Mohammed Siraj," said Gavaskar.Gavaskar on India's playing XIDespite raising questions over Jadeja's exclusion, Gavaskar backed the team picked by the management. He said that once the playing XI is announced, everyone should support the team and hope for a good performance."Siraj is the top wicket-taker in this cycle, but let's wait and see. I have always seen it this way: whatever reservations you might have regarding the final XI, 14, or 16, once the team is selected, it is your team and mine. It is the Indian team, after all. So, I am backing this team, and I am praying that this team does well," he added.Gurnoor Brar makes Test debutMeanwhile, India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl first in the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch.India made one change to their playing XI, handing a Test debut to pacer Gurnoor Brar. articles.title: 'Is he crying?': Mohammed Siraj's live TV visuals spark reaction from Ajinkya Rahane, Murali Kartik - WATCH
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Mohammed Siraj appeared visibly emotional after being left out of India's playing XI for the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Mohammed Siraj appeared visibly emotional after being left out of India's playing XI for the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch. The Indian fast bowler was spotted covering his eyes with sunglasses as cameras captured him on the opening morning at Hagley Oval.The visuals caught the attention of former India batter Ajinkya Rahane and ex-spinner Murali Kartik, who were on live commentary. Both spoke about Siraj's reaction, with Kartik suggesting that the decision to drop him would have hurt the pacer.Siraj's omission has also raised questions, especially considering his record in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle.Rahane, Kartik react to Siraj's live TV visualsRahane was quick to notice Siraj covering his eyes with his sunglasses when the visuals appeared during the broadcast."These visuals," Kartik said before Rahane asked, "Is he crying?"Kartik agreed that the fast bowler looked upset and explained that players react differently when they are left out of the team. He felt Siraj was someone who always wanted to be on the field and give his best."I don't know, brother. He certainly looks quite emotional to me, because he is an emotional person," Kartik began."Obviously, it hurts. Look, we have always played alongside all kinds of players; some are okay with it; there are some people who are fine when you drop them. And then there are some people who just want to play; it doesn't matter to them if they have pain in their leg, pain in their head, pain in their body, or shivering, they'll give everything they've got. They put their life on the line. He seems like that kind of bowler," he said."Because look, I don't know, sometimes you hide inside the hurt you must be feeling," he said."Because he was benched in the ODIs as well, and even during the West Indies tour that happened in India, he was only given a chance in the final match when they didn't want to play anyone else. This hurts a player," Kartik added.Kartik also said Siraj's performances and numbers made his exclusion even more difficult to understand."With the numbers you've seen so far, I am surprised, for what reason? Either don't keep him in the team at all then!" he argued."If you feel his form isn't good, or he's not bowling well in the nets, or wherever, I don't know whatever the thinking might be, then don't take him on the tour at all. Don't take him; what's the point then?"Siraj is India's leading wicket-taker in the ongoing WTC cycle, with 43 wickets from 11 matches.India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl first on a green-looking pitch at Hagley Oval. The team made one change to its pace attack, leaving out Prasidh Krishna and handing a Test debut to 26-year-old Punjab pacer Gurnoor Brar. articles.title: Akash Deep steals the show as New Zealand finish Day 1 of 2nd Test at 246/5
articles.summary: Akash Deep emerged as India's standout bowler on the opening day of the second Test against New Zealand, producing two outstanding deliveries in the
articles.body: Akash Deep emerged as India's standout bowler on the opening day of the second Test against New Zealand, producing two outstanding deliveries in the post-lunch session to overshadow even the impressive Jasprit Bumrah. New Zealand, however, recovered towards the end of the day to finish at 246/5 after 85 overs at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Friday.The two teams shared the honours, with New Zealand enjoying the first and final sessions while India fought back strongly in the middle session.After winning the toss and electing to bowl, India initially struggled to make inroads as New Zealand captain Tom Latham and Devon Conway put together a 77-run opening partnership. The hosts appeared comfortable against India's four-pronged pace attack before debutant Gurnoor Brar provided the breakthrough with the final delivery before lunch.Brar, who returned figures of 1/52 from 19 overs, dismissed Conway for 31 to give India some momentum heading into the break.However, it was Akash Deep who changed the complexion of the contest after lunch. The Bengal pacer, who returned to international cricket following a lengthy rehabilitation period for a lower back stress injury, finished with figures of 2/52 from 21 overs and was arguably India's most threatening bowler.Operating with the semi-new Kookaburra ball, Akash produced two superb deliveries to remove the well-set Latham and Rachin Ravindra, both caught behind by Rishabh Pant.Latham, who had scored 59, was beaten by a delivery that pitched on a good length before straightening just enough to take the outside edge. Ravindra, meanwhile, managed just eight deliveries at the crease before another testing delivery from Akash found his edge, with Pant completing the catch.In between those dismissals, Anshul Kamboj, whose selection had attracted considerable debate, accounted for Henry Nicholls. The left-hander departed for 16, leaving New Zealand in trouble at 110/4 after having reached 77 without losing a wicket. Kamboj returned figures of 1/56 from 17 overs.With India sensing an opportunity to take control, Tom Blundell and Daryl Mitchell joined forces to stabilise the innings. The pair added 74 runs for the fifth wicket before Washington Sundar broke the partnership, having Mitchell caught by Dhruv Jurel at leg-slip for 31. Washington finished with 1/36 from nine overs.Blundell remained unbeaten on 53 off 117 deliveries, displaying considerable patience during a challenging phase for the hosts. He found an able partner in Glenn Phillips, who continued New Zealand's recovery with an unbeaten 36 off 64 balls. The duo added 62 runs without being separated for the sixth wicket, ensuring the hosts finished the day on a relatively comfortable note.While Akash's ability to extract movement off the surface made him India's most effective bowler, Brar also made a positive impression on his Test debut. His inclusion appeared to add greater bite to the attack, with the debutant looking considerably more incisive than Prasidh Krishna.The Hagley Oval surface offered assistance to both batters and bowlers. There was bounce, carry and seam movement for the pacers, but batters who got themselves in were also able to play their shots and find value through the off-side.Earlier, Bumrah had a chance to strike in the opening over itself when Latham was given out leg-before. However, the New Zealand skipper successfully overturned the decision through DRS, avoiding a third successive duck. Bumrah went wicketless, but maintained impressive control throughout his spell, conceding just 37 runs in 19 overs.New Zealand were cautious during the initial exchanges, but batting became considerably easier once the first hour had passed. Conway, who had initially adopted a watchful approach, opened up with a stylish off-drive against Akash before following it up with a flashy cut for another boundary in the pacer's next over.Brar was introduced into the attack in the 18th over and immediately brought additional pace and bounce into the contest. The opening pair reached their 50-run partnership in the 19th over and looked largely untroubled against India's pace battery.Just when New Zealand appeared to be building a substantial opening stand, Akash and Brar combined to turn the tide, giving India a foothold in the contest before Blundell and Phillips ensured the hosts finished the opening day on level terms.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nathan Lyon set to be dropped by Australia for first Test against New Zealand
articles.summary: Australia will reportedly make the big call to drop frontline spinner Nathan Lyon for their opening Test against New Zealand on December 9; Lyon has been Australia's mainstay spin option for 13 years
articles.body:
Australia will name their squad on Saturday for the opening Test in Perth from December 9, but it seems the 39-year-old off-spinner will not be included.

A mainstay in the side, Lyon has been Australia's frontline spin option for over 13 years, taking 577 Test wickets from 145 matches.

Following his hamstring injury, which he suffered in the 2025 Ashes series, Lyon has begun to be more regularly omitted from the Test side.

Most recently, he missed Australia's second Test against South Africa when they opted to go for an all-pace bowling line-up.

In the rest of that tour, Lyon took six wickets at 43.67.

After Australia's loss to South Africa in Cape Town, in which South Africa spinner Simon Harmer took 6-16 in the second innings for victory, head coach Andrew McDonald was asked whether Lyon's position as Australia's continuous No 1 spinner would be assessed.

"I don't think it's something to review now," McDonald said. "We sit back and we'll go through Shield cricket. Nathan will be preparing for the first Test match in Perth."

Remarkably, until Australia's Test against West Indies in Jamaica in 2025, Lyon had not been left out of a squad since making his debut 15 years ago in 2011. He had also not missed a Test when available and fit since 2013.

articles.summary: Australia’s conduct is back under the microscope after Usman Khawaja’s stunning revelations in his autobiography
articles.body:
Australia's conduct during the 2017/18 Ashes is back under the microscope after the independent forum set up to explore the 'sandpapergate' scandal was handed an expanded brief.

Earlier this month, Cricket Australia reacted to a barrage of claims and counter-claims from former players by announcing that all players and staff members would be invited to share their recollections of the ill-fated 2018 South Africa tour in a 'safe space'.

CA has now formalised the terms of reference and opted to add the previous home summer – when Australia beat England 4-0 to reclaim the urn – to its scope.

A statement confirmed the forum would hear accounts related to "ball-management practices in the Australian Men's Team during the 2017/18 season, all four Tests of the 2018 SA Tour, the events of 24 March 2018, (and) the conduct and scope of the 2018 CA investigation".

Usman Khawaja , whose autobiography reopened the historic drama , has alleged that ball-tampering methods were being utilised prior to South Africa and Cameron Bancroft – who was caught red-handed in Cape Town with sandpaper – has written about being urged to manipulate the quarter-seam on his Test debut against England in Brisbane.

Those claims have brought to light a passage in Sir Alastair Cook's own memoir, published in 2019, in which he alleges David Warner admitted during a post-series drink to using substances in his finger strapping to deteriorate the ball.

CA has reiterated its previous commitment that no new sanctions or punishments will be handed down, while the confidentiality of all participants has been guaranteed.

After a six-week evidence period, a report will be published within 30 days covering "principal themes" and "recommendations for future improvements" rather than specific testimony or direct apportioning of blame.

"We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn.
